result.summary: The street environment provides basic pedestrian access with sidewalks on both sides, though they are narrow and obstructed by utility poles on the right. The lack of marked crossings and the presence of parked cars that obscure sightlines create a moderately hazardous environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles are located directly in the path of the right-side sidewalk, significantly reducing the effective walking width.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the street along the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous on-street parallel parking obscures sightlines between pedestrians and drivers, especially near the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility patterns to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Widen the sidewalk or relocate utility poles to ensure a clear, ADA-compliant walking path.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow residential street lined with row houses and parallel parked cars. While a continuous sidewalk is present, there is no buffer between the walkway and the roadway, and parked vehicles create significant visual obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street obscures sightlines between drivers and pedestrians, particularly children, who might step into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and background along the curb line

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: An orange construction barrel is placed on the sidewalk, narrowing the effective walking width.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the sidewalk in front of the red brick building

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Removing parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Greenery
interventions.description: Installing street trees or planters to provide a physical buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway while improving the pedestrian environment.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Extending the sidewalk into the parking lane at intersections or mid-block to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow urban street with parallel parking on both sides and buildings situated directly at the sidewalk edge. While continuous sidewalks are present, they are narrow and lack a buffer from the roadway, and the dense line of parked vehicles creates significant visual obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the narrow street blocks sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Narrow Walkways
hazards.description: The sidewalks are relatively narrow and lack a buffer zone, placing pedestrians in close proximity to parked and moving vehicles.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near intersections or mid-block crossing points to improve sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Marked Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add high-visibility marked crosswalks to designate safe crossing locations and alert drivers to pedestrian presence.

result.summary: The image shows a continuous, paved sidewalk in good condition along a mixed-use urban street with buildings situated directly at the walkway edge. While the sidewalk is of adequate width, there is no physical buffer from the roadway, and parked vehicles create potential visual obstructions for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Visual obstruction from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block the line of sight between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground and mid-ground along the curb line.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-vehicle separation
hazards.description: There is no physical buffer, such as a planting strip or furniture zone, between the sidewalk and the travel lane.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the entire visible length of the sidewalk edge.
